issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodos function - user input directly interpolated into SQL query
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE title LIKE $1 OR description LIKE $1'; await db.query(query, [`%${keyword}%`]);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in searchTodosByStatus - user input concatenated without validation or parameterization
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT * FROM todos WHERE completed = $1'; await db.query(query, [completed === 'true']);

issues.description: SQL injection vulnerability in getTodosByUser - userId directly embedded in template literal without parameterization
issues.suggestion: Use parameterized query: const query = 'SELECT t.* FROM todos t JOIN user_todos ut ON t.id = ut.todo_id WHERE ut.user_id = $1'; await db.query(query, [userId]);

issues.description: HTML entity encoding is insufficient for XSS prevention in all contexts - doesn't handle script contexts, URL contexts, or advanced attack vectors
issues.suggestion: Use a well-tested sanitization library like DOMPurify or validator.js, or implement context-aware encoding. For display, consider using framework-provided escaping (React, Vue, etc.)

issues.description: generateId() uses Date.now() and Math.random() which are not cryptographically secure and may produce collisions under high concurrency
issues.suggestion: Use crypto.randomUUID() for secure, collision-resistant IDs: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return randomUUID(); }

issues.description: Error handling in createTodo throws generic error - lacks specific error types making it hard for callers to handle different failure scenarios
issues.suggestion: Create custom error classes (ValidationError, DatabaseError) and throw appropriate types: if (!validateTodoInput(input)) { throw new ValidationError('Invalid todo input', { field: 'title' }); }

issues.description: No error handling for database operations - db.query() could throw but errors are not caught or logged
issues.suggestion: Add try-catch blocks with proper error handling: try { await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { logger.error('Failed to create todo', error); throw new DatabaseError('Failed to create todo', { cause: error }); }

issues.description: getAllTodos assumes db.query returns rows directly without error checking or validating response structure
issues.suggestion: Add response validation: const result = await db.query(query); if (!result || !Array.isArray(result)) { throw new Error('Invalid database response'); } return result as Todo[];

issues.description: getTodoById uses array length check instead of optional chaining or more idiomatic approach
issues.suggestion: Use optional chaining: const result = await db.query(query, [id]); return result?.[0] ?? null;

issues.description: updateTodoStatus doesn't verify if the todo exists before updating, silently succeeds even if no rows affected
issues.suggestion: Check affected rows and return boolean or throw: const result = await db.query(query, [completed, id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new NotFoundError('Todo not found'); }

issues.description: deleteTodo doesn't verify if todo exists or return success indicator, making it impossible to distinguish between successful deletion and no-op
issues.suggestion: Check affected rows and return boolean or throw: const result = await db.query(query, [id]); if (result.rowCount === 0) { throw new NotFoundError('Todo not found'); } return true;

issues.description: sanitizeInput is applied to description even when empty string, unnecessary processing
issues.suggestion: Apply sanitization conditionally: const sanitizedDescription = input.description ? sanitizeInput(input.description) : '';

issues.description: validateTodoInput performs multiple checks but doesn't provide specific error messages about what failed
issues.suggestion: Return validation result object: return { valid: boolean, errors: string[] } to help callers provide better user feedback

issues.description: searchTodosByStatus accepts string parameter but should accept boolean, allowing invalid values like 'yes', 'no', '1 OR 1=1'
issues.suggestion: Change parameter type to boolean: export async function searchTodosByStatus(completed: boolean): Promise<Todo[]> and use parameterized query

issues.description: Missing database module import validation - if './database' doesn't export 'db', this will fail at runtime
issues.suggestion: Add runtime check or use type imports: import type { Database } from './database'; and verify db is properly initialized

codeQuality.summary: This file contains 3 CRITICAL SQL injection vulnerabilities (lines 126, 136, 146) that must be fixed immediately. All three use string concatenation/interpolation instead of parameterized queries, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands. Additional issues include weak ID generation using Math.random() instead of crypto.randomUUID(), insufficient XSS protection relying on basic HTML entity encoding, missing error handling for database operations, and functions that don't verify operation success (update/delete). The code demonstrates good intentions with parameterized queries in some functions but critically fails in search operations. Fix the SQL injection vulnerabilities immediately, improve error handling, use secure ID generation, and add operation verification checks.

testCoverage.summary: No tests found for src/todo.ts. The file contains 10 exported functions with 0% test coverage. Critical security vulnerabilities exist in 3 functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) that use SQL injection-prone string concatenation instead of parameterized queries. These MUST be tested immediately to prevent production exploits. The secure functions (createTodo, getTodoById, updateTodoStatus, deleteTodo) use proper parameterized queries but lack test coverage. Input validation and sanitization functions (validateTodoInput, sanitizeInput) are untested despite being critical for security. Recommended priority: 1) Test SQL injection vulnerabilities, 2) Test validation/sanitization, 3) Test CRUD operations, 4) Test edge cases.

refactorings.summary: The code is well-structured but has several refactoring opportunities. Key improvements include: (1) implementing the Repository pattern to separate data access from business logic, (2) modernizing validation to return descriptive errors instead of booleans, (3) using optional chaining and nullish coalescing for cleaner null handling, (4) extracting SQL queries into constants, (5) optimizing the sanitizeInput function with a map-based approach, and (6) extracting the todo factory logic. The vulnerable SQL injection functions (searchTodos, searchTodosByStatus, getTodosByUser) are intentionally flawed per the code comments and should not be refactored here - those are security issues, not structural improvements. Overall impact: medium to high - these changes would significantly improve maintainability, testability, and code clarity.
